name: the-confirmation-toast-follows-the-notification-timeout-step
description:
PushNotificationTimeoutToSidebar pushed atriumSetNotificationTimeout into the sidebar document only. The confirmation toast lives on its own document (ToastOverlayWidget, toast-surface.js) and never heard the setting, so atriumConfirmToast always fell back to toast-stack.js's CONFIRM_MS (1400ms) no matter what Settings said.

This drives the real gesture twice with two different steps in one session, then a third time with the step off, and grades every leg by timing rather than pixels - the same DOM-polling method copy-link-confirmation.json already established for this exact widget. The Notification timeout row is a plain <select> (six choices, not in SEGMENTED_CHOICE_ROWS), and settings-choice-and-number.json already recorded that a synthetic mouse click cannot drive a native <select> popup in this harness; the select's value is set and its change event dispatched directly instead, which still runs the real settings.js commitControl -> setRow -> chrome.send('settingsChanged', ...) path, not a hand-rolled push.

LEG ONE (threeSeconds). Set the row, close Settings (its own key focus would otherwise eat the copy chord - profiles-pane-two-engines.json's cmd+w note), copy the link. The toast is checked still up at ~1.8s (past the old CONFIRM_MS default) and gone by ~5.3s (past 3000ms plus the .bye fade) - so this also covers the 'on load' half, since this is the FIRST confirmation of the session and the toast document is built lazily on first use, right here.

LEG TWO (tenSeconds), same window, same session. The toast is checked still up past 3.8s - the point the FIRST leg's step would already have dismissed it, proving the second push actually took effect rather than the widget keeping the first value - and gone by ~12.8s.

LEG THREE (off). The native ShowTransientConfirmation path always logs 'confirmation shown', so the log line cannot distinguish a suppressed toast from a shown one; the DOM card is what is graded, and it must never exist.
